   City Council Special Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, December 6, 2022

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Rivera

  Rivera, Wu

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of November 15, 2022.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of November 15, 2022.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented

  CEQA Determination: Not a Project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 6, 2022  2
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. 2023 CITY COUNCIL MEETING SCHEDULE

  The City Council is scheduled to meet regularly on the first and third Tuesdays
  of each month. In the past, meeting cancellations have been decided on as the
  year progresses, due to holidays and/or lack of business items. There are
  nominal savings in staff time and utility costs for cancelled meetings.

  CEQA Determination: Not a Project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA
  Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the 2023 City Council meeting
  schedule.

  D. DEVELOPMENT IMPACT FEE COMPLIANCE REPORT REQUIRED PURSUANT
  TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 66006 FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021-2022

  Pursuant to Government Code Section 66066, a local agency which levies a fee
  subject to Government Code Section 66001 shall make available to the public
  a report providing the information required by Government Code Section
  66006(b)(1) and shall review that information at the next public meeting not
  less than 15 days after the information has been made available to the public.
  There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  CEQA Determination: Not a Project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA
  Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council receive and file the Annual Development
  Impact Fee Compliance Report for Fiscal Year 2021-2022 in accordance with
  Government Code Section 66006.

  E. RESOLUTION NO. 22-72 AMENDING THE AUTHORIZED SALARY
  SCHEDULE TO INCORPORATE THE CALIFORNIA MINIMUM WAGE RATE

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 6, 2022  3
   On January 1, 2023, the State minimum wage will increase by 3.5% to $15.50
  per hour. Senate Bill 3 (“SB 3”), which was approved in 2016, gradually raised
  the minimum wage to $15.00 per hour by January 1, 2022 for employers with
  26 or more employees. For 2023, the state minimum wage is scheduled to be
  increased by the national Consumer Price Index (CPI) or 3.5%, whichever is less.
  Due to a historically high CPI for the past fiscal year, the minimum wage will be
  increased by 3.5% to $15.50 per hour in 2023. The minimum wage and equity
  adjustments are expected to have an annualized cost impact of $153,098.

  CEQA Determination: Not a Project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA
  Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-72, which
  amends the City’s Authorized Salary Schedule by increasing the pay rage of all
  part-time position classifications by the 2023 minimum wage rate requirement
  and applying an equity adjustment to the pay range of all regular non-
  represented full-time positions except for the Police Captain, effective
  December 31, 2022, and increases General Fund appropriations by $57,118 and
  various other special funds $19,431 to cover increased costs to salaries and
  benefits for Fiscal Year 2022-2023.

  F. RESOLUTION NO. 22-74 RATIFYING THE MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING WITH THE SAN GABRIEL FIRE MANAGEMENT GROUP
  FOR THE JULY 1, 2022 THROUGH JUNE 30, 2025 PERIOD AND
  INCREASING GENERAL FUND APPROPRIATIONS FOR FIRE MANAGEMENT
  SALARIES

  The most recent Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the City and
  the Fire Management Group (FMG) expired on June 30, 2022. Representatives
  of the City and FMG have conferred and reached agreement over a successor
  MOU for the period covering July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2025. The successor
  MOU with FMG is expected to have a total three-year cost impact of $691,741,
  of which $175,677 is for Fiscal Year 2022-2023, $239,873 is for Fiscal Year 2023-
  2024, and $276,191 is for Fiscal Year 2024-25.

  CEQA Determination: Not a Project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA
  Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 6, 2022  4
   Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-74, which
  approves the three-year successor MOU for the period covering July 1, 2022,
  through June 30, 2025, between the City and FMG and increases General Fund
  appropriations $175,677 to cover increased costs to Fire Management salaries
  in Fiscal Year 2022-2023.

  G. PURCHASE OF AN ELEVATOR (ARM) ATTACHMENT IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $17,486.55 FOR AN EXISTING SEWER INSPECTION CAMERA CRAWLER
  FOR THE WASTEWATER OPERATIONS DIVISION

  The Wastewater Operations Division within the Public Works Department is
  responsible for the operation and maintenance of the City’s sewer and storm
  water systems. The sewer system consists of 72 miles of sewer main lines as well
  as 1,350 maintenance holes. The Wastewater Operations Division has the need
  of an elevator (Arm) attachment to improve the functionality of the sewer
  inspection camera in deep sewage conditions or in larger pipes. The total
  amount of the Rovver X Elevator (Arm) Attachment for the existing Inspection
  Camera Crawler is $17,486.55, which can be supported by the adopted Fiscal
  Year 2022-23 Budget by sewer account 137-800-01-21-000.

  CEQA Determination: Not a Project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA
  Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Cooperative Purchase
  Agreement for the purchase of a Rovver X Elevator (Arm) Attachment,
  consistent with the piggyback bidding requirements pursuant to Municipal
  Code Section 34.35; and authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase
  Order with Haaker Equipment Company in the amount not to exceed
  $17,486.55 from budget account 137-800-01-21-000.

  H. COUNTYWIDE HOUSEHOLD HAZARDOUS COLLECTION PROGRAM SITING
  LIABILITY AGREEMENT WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY

  The County of Los Angeles and the Los Angeles County Sanitation District have
  reserved Saturday, January 7, 2023, to co-host an Annual Countywide
  Household Hazardous and Electronic Waste collection event at the Mission
  Playhouse Parking Lot in San Gabriel. The event will accept qualifying waste
  from participants who show proof of Los Angeles County residency from 9:00
  a.m. to 3:00 p.m. on the day of the event. There is no fiscal impact related to
  this item.

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 6, 2022  5
   CEQA Determination: Not a Project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA
  Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the Countywide Household Hazardous Waste Collection Program Siting
  Liability Agreement.

  I. 2023 LUNAR NEW YEAR FESTIVAL

  Since 2016, the City of San Gabriel has hosted a Lunar New Year Festival in the
  Mission District. For the 2023 event, celebrating the Year of the Rabbit, staff is
  recommending that the city work with media partner MRBI/KAZN (KAZN) to
  host the Lunar New Year celebration proposed to be held on Saturday, February
  4 from 10:00 am to 9:00 pm. As part of the FY 22-23 budget, the City Council
  allocated funding for community engagement events with a portion of that
  funding designated for the 8th Annual Lunar New Year Festival. With the event
  being hosted by KAZN, event costs will be significantly lower with the city
  funding only the opening gathering for dignitaries.

  CEQA Determination: Not a Project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA
  Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the proposal and the draft
  Professional Services Agreement to authorize KAZN to host the 2023 Lunar
  New Year Festival and authorize the City Manager to sign the final agreement,
  subject to its approval by the City Attorney.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS – None.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 6, 2022  6

MINUTES OF DECEMBER 6, 2022

I  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

  CALL TO ORDER

  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  John R. Harrington, and Mayor Tony Ding .
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith

I  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,
  Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark,
  Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg de Vinck, Fire
  Chief  Steven  Wallace,  Human  Resources/Risk

  Development Director Aldo Cervantes, and Assistant

I  Association, San Gabriel Fire Management Group, and all Unrepresented

I  City Manager Lazzaretto made the presentation .

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR
